description: The PROCESSOR prompt shape checkpoint 168 was validated on (tuning/producer_v3/evaluation_protocol.json, 84 DEV rows, contract validity 1.0): the compact extraction contract followed by this semantic policy as the SYSTEM message, and one canonical JSON object (context_only_spans, production_contract, required_refs, role, routed_rules, source_spans, supplied_refs; sorted keys, compact separators) as the USER message, through the model's own chat template. compact_contracts.validated_messages builds exactly that for every bounded partition; nothing else reaches the model on that path. The suffix is the frozen renderer's text (tuning/first_domain_agnostic_v1/common.py messages()) and is never typed into a script: check 263 renders a DEV row through the runtime builder and requires the protocol's recorded prompt sha256 byte for byte, so drift here refuses the gate.
system_suffix:
Use producer-semantic-policy-v3 canonical Gap/Uncertainty JSON strings. Preserve absence, temporal role, order/content and epistemic distinctions. Structural headings alone are not propositions. Each Gap/Uncertainty object has category, subject, attribute, ordinal, relation, state, scope and unit; use exact finite policy values.
Finite attributes: authorization_time,date_unspecified,effective_time,entry_content,entry_order,entry_presence,event_occurrence,event_time,interpretation,observation_time,ratification_status,recorder,recording_occurrence,recording_time,reporting_time,submission_occurrence,submission_time. Gap categories: missing_information, explicit_question, explicit_nonoccurrence; uncertainty category: unknown. Subjects: owned_record, entry, amendment, submission, event. Ordinal: null,1,2,3,next,previous,later. State: unspecified,requested,absent,not_recorded,not_submitted,did_not_occur,unknown. scope=owned_record; relation=null; unit=null. Canonical strings begin Gap: or Uncertainty: followed by the JSON object. Conflict is not epistemic uncertainty; absence is not unknown occurrence; recording, event, submission and authorization times differ. Order differs from content; first, next, previous and later retain their source meanings.
inline_reference_markers: Every indexed passage inside a source span is shown as ' (REF-NNNN)' at the passage's end, the way the training spans carried their references; Python decides which passages lie in which span from the reference index (bounded_extraction.grounding) and the same decision is the validator's citable set.
